correctness.rationale: For every existing generalized hexagon of equal order \(q\ge2\) the incidence axiom fixes the six-shell intersection array, the seven adjacency eigenvalues, and the powered-distance eigenvalue on each sector. Exact tail formulas compare each nonparity eigenvalue strictly below the parity eigenvalue for \(0<p\le1\) using two elementary adjacent-increment ratio bounds and explicit order-two exceptions. The parity scalar is -1 at \(p=0\) and strictly positive at \(p=1\); the first zero is non-strict negative type, while Li–Weston strictness excludes every larger endpoint. Schoenberg Gram rank is \(N-1\) below and \(N-2\) at the root. Uniform Taylor expansion gives the \(q^{-5}\) and \(q^{-6}\) terms. The standalone symbolic verifier checks the recurrence, shell coefficients, bounds on sampled integer orders, and high-precision roots; the universal proof is analytic, not based on finite experiments.

value.rationale: The generalized-hexagon incidence graph is the canonical girth-twelve member of finite generalized polygon geometry. The exact all-order negative-type threshold, rigid one-dimensional point–line equality space, critical Euclidean dimension, and quintic exponent collapse resolve a motivated metric embedding invariant across an infinite family, not an arbitrarily selected numerical instance. The novel work is the uniform ordering and asymptotic description rather than routine use of the distance-regular recurrence.
